in_hebrew.name: קריתה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A feminine name derived from the Hebrew word קרית (kirit), meaning 'meadow, pasture, village'. It can be interpreted as 'village girl' or 'maiden of the meadow'. In the Bible, the name Karita is not found, but it is related to the name Kira, which is mentioned in the Book of Esther as a noblewoman in the Persian court.

in_greek.name: Καρίτα
in_greek.long_meaning: A Greek name derived from the word καριτης (karitēs), meaning 'pure, virgin'. In the Bible, the name Karita is not found, but it is related to the name Kariode, which is mentioned in the New Testament as the name of a woman who was healed by Jesus.

in_latin.name: Karita
in_latin.long_meaning: A Latin name derived from the word karitas, meaning 'pure, clear'. In the Bible, the name Karita is not found, but it is related to the name Kara, which is mentioned in the Vulgate as the name of a woman who was healed by Jesus.
